meta.title: Daniel Reed | Keynote speaker for conferences and summits
meta.description: Demo site for a fictional keynote speaker. Talks of 20 to 60 minutes on stage or live online, on decisions, uncertainty and experiments.

rationale: Портрет стоит в первом экране рядом с заголовком и одной кнопкой «Explore the talks», а холодный светлый фон и оранжевый акцент вырастают из сине-серого фона фото. Три темы вынесены в крупный нумерованный указатель на тёмной полосе, чтобы организатор сравнивал их с одного взгляда, а ниже короткий диалог вопрос-ответ помогает выбрать тему и формат без формы и личных контактов.

props.headline: Daniel Reed, keynote speaker
props.sub: Keynotes for conferences, summits and company events, on stage or live online. Three talks to choose from, and a workshop on the same day if we discuss it.

photo.subject: Portrait of Daniel Reed, a dark curly-haired man in a navy jacket against a slate-blue background

props.caption: minutes. A keynote on stage or live online.

props.title: Three talks
props.intro: Each one works as a keynote of 20 to 60 minutes. Pick the topic closest to what your audience deals with.

items.name: How teams make decisions
items.description: A look at how a group gets from several options to one choice: who is heard, how options are weighed and how the decision is agreed. For audiences who work and decide together.

items.name: Working through uncertainty
items.description: A talk about carrying on when facts are incomplete and plans keep shifting, and how people and teams can act sensibly without waiting for certainty.

items.name: Turning ideas into experiments
items.description: How to take an idea and shape it into a small test that can be run, observed and learned from, before anyone commits to the whole thing.

pairs.answer: Either. Daniel speaks on stage at your event or live online.
Yes, if it is discussed. A workshop can run on the same day as the keynote.
Decisions suits people who work in teams and have to agree. Uncertainty suits audiences facing change. Experiments suits those with ideas still waiting to be tried.
